notes: All 19 years are IFRS as issued by the IASB; there is no change of standard basis, but several first-time adoptions restated the prior-year comparatives (see the restated flags on FY2007, FY2008, FY2012, FY2013, FY2014, FY2017, FY2020).

FY2007 is taken from the 2008 Reference Document and covers continuing operations only: Sagem Communications and Sagem Mobile Phones were presented as discontinued/disposal groups, so FY2007 revenue (€9,714m) and net income (€39m) exclude them.
FY2008 in the 2009 registration document is restated from the 2008 document's figures (profit from operations €603m then, €617m as restated).
IAS 19 revised adopted in 2013: the 2013 document restated FY2012 (equity €5,834m, operating income €1,187m).

IFRS 11 adopted in 2014: the 2014 document re-presented FY2013 and further restated the FY2012 balance sheet (total assets €22,674m, cash €2,083m). FY2012 balance-sheet values stored here are the 2013 document's, i.e. before that second restatement; the FY2012 income statement and cash flow were not changed by IFRS 11.

IFRS 15 adopted in 2018: FY2017 as originally published in the 2017 document was revenue €16,940m, profit from operations €2,681m, net income €4,790m and equity €10,321m; the values stored are the 2018 document's restated comparatives.
IFRS 16 adopted in 2019 with no restatement of 2018.
operatingCashFlow is the 'TOTAL I' line (net cash provided by operating activities), i.e. after changes in working capital, not Safran's 'cash flow from operations' before working-capital changes.

totalDebt is non-current plus current interest-bearing financial liabilities per the balance-sheet note; it excludes 'borrowings subject to specific conditions' (repayable advances, about €1.0bn in 2025), which is why it sits below third-party total-debt figures.

capex is purchases of property, plant and equipment only, stored negative. Safran reports purchases of intangible assets (about €0.6bn in 2025) on a separate cash-flow line, so this figure is lower than a capex measure that adds intangibles.

operatingIncome is the statutory 'Profit from operations' line. Safran also publishes 'adjusted' figures that exclude the effect of hedge accounting on revenue and profit; those are not used anywhere in this file.
FY2019 dividendPerShare is 0: the €2.38 per share dividend in respect of 2019 was cancelled by the Board in 2020 because of Covid-19, so nothing was paid in respect of that year.
FY2025 dividendPerShare of €3.35 is the dividend proposed by the Board and subject to shareholder approval.

employees is the group headcount at 31 December used in Safran's operational reporting. From 2024 the URD also publishes a wider CSRD scope (103,058 for 2024 and 110,778 for 2025) that differs from the 99,364 and 110,535 stored here.

Yahoo cross-check, FY2022-FY2025 (snapshot 2026-10-26, USD divided by average rates of about 1.05, 1.09, 1.08 and 1.13): revenue and net income agree within roughly 1% in all four years, which confirms the statutory revenue line rather than Safran's adjusted revenue (e.g. €31,329m adjusted versus €31,189m statutory for 2025).
